learning_objective: 🎯 Upgrade your accounting system! When a business grows, one Journal isn't enough. Learn how to use special books for Cash, Purchases, and Sales.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is a special book that records ONLY cash and bank transactions. It serves as both a Journal and a Ledger account. If a transaction has no cash/bank involved, it does NOT go in the Cash Book.
When you deposit cash into the bank, or withdraw cash from the bank for office use, it affects both Cash and Bank columns simultaneously. This is called a Contra entry, marked with a tiny 'C'.
To save time, we use specific books: 'Purchases Book' (only for CREDIT purchases of goods), 'Sales Book' (only for CREDIT sales of goods), and 'Return Books'.
Used for recording small, daily expenses like tea, postage, and stationery. The head cashier gives a fixed amount (Imprest amount) to the petty cashier at the start of the month to manage these.

fun_activity.title: 🪙 The Imprest System Game
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine your mom gives you ₹500 at the start of the week for small school expenses (Imprest amount). You spend ₹300 by Friday. On Sunday, she gives you exactly ₹300 back so you start Monday with ₹500 again. That's exactly how a Petty Cash Book works!

exam_tips: 📌 The Purchases Book records ONLY credit purchases of 'Goods' (items you trade in). If you buy Machinery on credit, it goes to the Journal Proper, not the Purchases Book!
📌 Trade Discount is NEVER recorded in the books of accounts; it is deducted directly from the invoice price. Cash Discount IS recorded.
📌 Remember that drawing cash from the bank for PERSONAL use is 'Drawings' and not a Contra entry.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Cash Book records all cash receipts and payments and acts as a principal book.
⭐ Special purpose books (subsidiary books) divide the journal to handle large volumes of transactions.
⭐ The Petty Cash Book handles minor expenses using the Imprest System to save the head cashier's time.
